 Upper level ridging through the day on Saturday will help to 
maintain well above normal temperatures across all of the Northern 
Rockies, with high temperatures peaking on Saturday as increasing 
flow and strong warm air advection brings readings into the mid-90s 
to near 110 degrees. While overall dry conditions will persist 
beneath this ridge there remains enough monsoonal moisture spreading 
north and east across portions of Southwest and into Central Montana 
to support isolated to widely scattered showers and thunderstorms 
during the afternoon and evening hours through Friday. Biggest 
impact from the showers and thunderstorms will be gusty and erratic 
outflow winds. By Saturday night the upper level ridge will be 
broken down by a potent upper level trough sliding east across 
Southern Canada, with this trough and attendant (dry) cold front 
brining gusty winds to all areas for the day on Sunday and below 
temperatures for the day on Monday. - Moldan

- Forecast Confidence & Scenarios:

Return of Extreme Temperatures by Saturday...

Climate anomaly indicators remain honed in on Saturday being the 
hottest day of the upcoming week, with ECMWF EFI values peaking 
between 0.75 and 0.9 across Southwest through North Central Montana; 
which continues to suggest unusual to very unusual hot temperatures 
with respect to early August climatology. This is remarkable 
considering that August 1st is only one day removed from the 
climatological peak for average high temperatures across Southwest 
through North Central Montana. 

The table below represents the potential high temperature scenarios 
for select cities across Southwest through North Central Montana, 
with the "Low End" scenario being the NBM10Pct (10% chance that 
temperatures are lower than the listed value), "Most Likely" 
scenario being the NBM50Pct, and the "High End" scenario being the 
NBM90Pct (10% chance that temperatures exceed the listed value).

While wildfire smoke can significantly influence high temperatures 
by limit heating...the past few days have only seen minor impacts to 
forecasted highs. Therefore the earlier (in the week) concerns that 
I had on forecasted highs being held below the 50Pct, or "Most 
Likely" scenario, on Saturday have decreased. Given this increased 
confidence in hot temperatures occurring on Saturday, most notably 
over portions of the Central and North Central Montana plains, an 
Extreme Heat Watch has been issued from 18z Saturday through 18z 
Sunday due to the hot daytime temperatures and limited cooling (as 
compared to climatology) during the overnight hours. 

High Winds from Saturday night through Sunday morning...

H700 winds of 40-60kts, which is an impressive 3 to nearly 4 
standard deviations above normal per NAEFS analysis, are prog'd to 
overspread the Rocky Mountain Front from 00z Sunday through 18z 
Sunday. BUFKIT soundings support ideal thermal profiles, especially 
between 06z and 14z Sunday, for mountain wave activity across the 
Eastern Glacier Park Region out to Cut Bank. This anomalous cross 
barrier flow combined with the potential for mountain wave activity 
has increased concerns that High Winds could materialize across all 
of Glacier County and portions of western Toole and central Pondera 
Counties. For this reason a High Wind Watch has been issued from 03z 
Sunday through 18z Sunday for these areas, with the most concerning 
timeframe being between 06-14z Sunday. Those looking to travel or 
recreate along the Rocky Mountain Front should be prepared for 
strong winds; which could make driving and hiking difficult, lead to 
falling trees in the backcountry, and/or lead to the spread of 
existing/new wildfires.
